title: The assistant can tell you something is ready

steps.path: A reply where the assistant flagged something for you
steps.headline: The assistant's notification is its own card in the chat, glowing blue until you click it.
steps.changed: When the assistant notifies you, its short label and message show as a blue card at the end of its reply. Before, the same call would have been a grey tool line saying "NotifyUser".
steps.notice: The card stands out from the reply around it. Clicking it stops the glow; the card stays, plain, so you can find it again. The click is remembered after a restart.
steps.risk: The glow is the only "unread" mark: if you read the card without clicking it, it keeps glowing until you do. Clicking is remembered per device, so your phone and computer each track their own.

steps.path: A conversation where the assistant notified you, then kept writing
steps.headline: A "Jump to notification" button appears when the card is out of sight.
steps.changed: The button sits where "Jump to bottom" does, in the same blue as the card. It shows only while the latest notification is unclicked and off screen; if both show, it sits just above "Jump to bottom".
steps.notice: Here the assistant said "Slow tests fixed" and kept working, so the card scrolled away. One click scrolls back up to it.
steps.risk: It only points at the latest notification since your last message; older ones still glow but have no button.

steps.path: The list of conversations (the arrow beside the session names)
steps.headline: The conversation's status says the assistant's own words, like "Slow tests fixed", in blue.
steps.changed: The second row said "Working" in green. Now it shows the assistant's label with a blue light, even though it is still working, until you open that conversation.
steps.notice: You can tell which conversation wants you, and why, without opening it. Opening it puts the light back to normal.
steps.risk: While the label shows, you can't see from the list that it is still working. Labels longer than about three words are cut short with "…".

steps.path: The same reply, on a phone
steps.headline: On a phone the card fits the narrow chat the same way.
steps.changed: Same card, its message wrapping to the phone's width.
steps.notice: Your phone also shows the label in its list of conversations, the same as the computer.
